subject: Data Engineering
title: Amazon Redshift's Evolution
description: A short lesson to help you apply Amazon Redshift's Evolution.

hook.text: Redshift was the first major cloud warehouse, launched by AWS in 2012. It changed the game.

buildup.text: Early Redshift used fixed clusters — you chose a size and paid whether you used it or not.

discovery.text: Redshift Serverless and RA3 nodes later added storage-compute separation, catching up to Snowflake.

twist.text: Redshift's tight AWS integration is a strength for AWS shops but creates lock-in for multi-cloud teams.

climax.text: Redshift proved the cloud warehouse market existed, then had to evolve as competitors leapfrogged it.

punchline.text: First to market doesn't mean first to finish.

quiz.question: What was a limitation of early Amazon Redshift?
options: Fixed clusters that you paid for regardless of usage
